text:
Leah: FYI - HeliosCare wants a 10-day Edgeflow POC: 7-day burst + 3-day reserved week. Procurement asks for a single PO covering both and says MSA must be exec-signed before they issue PO. Can we do PO-first?
Rafael (Legal): We got their MSA/DPA redlines. They added a clause that disallows any caching without prior written consent and appended a SOC2 addendum request. That no-cache language will force us to turn off prefix/KV cache unless we agree an exception.
Ibrahim (Presales): Technically we can invoice as two line items under one PO. Quick draft pricing for this POC:
```
edgeflow-burst-7d: $7,000 flat
reserved-week-3d-equivalent: $1,800
estimate-embeds: 30k units
```
If caching is disabled, token usage goes up ~20-30% for chat-heavy flows.
Nina (Finance): Single PO is fine but PO must contain our legal name, remittance address, and EIN. Also note: revenue recognition needs separate invoice lines. Please confirm billing codes.
po-checker-bot: PO scan - missing vendor EIN and signature block. Recommend HeliosCare use our PO template: https://redwood.co/po-template. Attach vendor tax doc (W-9 or local equivalent).
Leah: @Rafael (Legal) - can we accept the DPA redline for a scoped POC? If they insist on exec-sig pre-PO, timeline slips.
Rafael (Legal): Not as-is. Propose an Appendix A scoped to the Edgeflow POC: limit caching to ephemeral in-memory KV, retention <= 10 days, no subprocessor transfers, and explicit opt-out after POC. Also request Security to confirm SOC2 addendum is acceptable for ephemeral access. If HeliosCare insists on exec-sign before PO, Sales Ops needs to trigger expedited countersign.
Ibrahim (Presales): For the quote, suggest two options to keep deal moving: (A) PO-first with Appendix limiting cache (increase trial units to cover worst-case), or (B) exec-sign-first to keep current rates. I'll prepare a revised order form showing both options.
Nina (Finance): Option A ok if PO includes vendor info and we get their invoice remittance details. Also add explicit GL codes in the order form.
Leah: I'll post the draft order form here. If procurement refuses the Appendix, we mark POC as "no-cache" and update presales estimate.
Rafael (Legal): Add this text snippet to Appendix A: "For the duration of the Edgeflow POC only, Redwood Inference may use ephemeral in-memory cache limited to KV entries that are expired within ten (10) days; no persistent or external subprocessor caching is permitted. This scope expires at POC termination." That should address their consent concern.
Ibrahim (Presales): I'll update the usage projection assuming +25% token consumption with cache off and attach a side-by-side table.
po-checker-bot: Reminder - include W-8/W-9 or local tax form and vendor contact. PO template: https://redwood.co/po-template#multi-line.
Leah: Plan: (1) Attach two-line-item order form with both options, (2) request Sales Ops e-sign fast-route if exec-sig required, (3) ping Security for SOC2 addendum quick thumbs-up. Back with draft in ~30m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Rafael (Legal): Thanks. If Sales Ops needs language for countersign routing, tell them to flag this as "PO-first - legal appendix pending" so finance doesn't block payment.
Nina (Finance): Will review once draft is uploaded. Keep me in the loop for GL codes and invoice sequencing.
Ibrahim (Presales): Uploading the updated estimate and order form next.
Leah: Thanks team — will follow up once Sales Ops confirms e-sign path.
